title: How to make a Pokémon GO trade list

sections.h: What this trade list generator does
sections.html:
The Pokémon GO Trade List Generator turns the Pokémon you are looking for and the ones you can give away into one clean image you can post in a Discord server, a Facebook group, a community chat or a Reddit thread. Instead of typing long lists by hand, you pick cards from a catalogue of every Pokémon combination in the game — shiny Pokémon, regional and seasonal forms, costumes, gender differences, Dynamax and Gigantamax, purified Pokémon, and Pokémon with location and special backgrounds.

It is free, needs no account and works on phones as well as on desktop browsers.

sections.h: Make your list in four steps
sections.html:
1. Add what you want. Under Looking For, tap ✏️ Add and search by name or Pokédex number. Filters narrow the grid to Shiny, Form/Costume, Dynamax, Gigantamax or Legendary Pokémon, and you can swipe sideways to select many cards at once.
  2. Add what you can offer. Do the same under For Trade. The Backgrounds tab lists Pokémon that appeared with location or event backgrounds, and Custom combo lets you build a combination the catalogue does not cover: any Pokémon plus a marker and a background.
  3. Fine-tune each card. Use the small buttons on a card to mark its gender or the Poké Ball it was caught in, so trade partners know exactly which one you mean.
  4. Make the image. Tap 🎨 Make image to choose a theme, fonts, colours and how many cards go in each row, add your Trainer Code if you want, then download or share the picture.

sections.h: What to put on your trade list
sections.html:
A good list shows the Pokémon other players cannot easily get themselves. Popular choices:

  • Shiny Pokémon, especially ones from past events and Community Days.
  • Regional Pokémon that can only be caught in certain parts of the world.
  • Costumes and event forms that are no longer available.
  • Pokémon with location or special backgrounds — the background stays after the trade.
  • Legendary Pokémon from raids (a Special Trade, see the costs below).
  • Trade evolutions: a traded Kadabra, Machoke, Graveler, Haunter, Boldore, Gurdurr, Karrablast, Shelmet, Phantump or Pumpkaboo evolves for 0 Candy, so many players look for them.

Shadow Pokémon and most Mythical Pokémon cannot be traded, and a Pokémon you received in a trade cannot be traded again — leave those off your list.

sections.h: How much Stardust does a trade cost?
sections.html:
Both players pay Stardust. A normal trade of a Pokémon already in the receiver's Pokédex costs 100 at any Friendship level. Special Trades — Legendary, Mythical, Ultra Beast, Purified and shiny Pokémon, or anything the receiver has not registered — cost much more, are limited to one per day, and need at least Good Friends.

Ultra Friends1001,6001,60080,000

Forever Friends get the same Special Trade discount as Best Friends (96%). Events sometimes cut trade costs further.

• Trading re-rolls a Pokémon's IVs. Higher Friendship raises the minimum; community data puts it at 1, 2, 3 and 5 for Good, Great, Ultra and Best Friends.
  • A Lucky Trade turns both Pokémon into Lucky Pokémon, with IVs of at least 12/12/12 (community data). Lucky Pokémon cost 50% less Stardust to power up.
  • Best Friends who keep interacting can become Lucky Friends: the next trade between them is guaranteed to be Lucky. A Lucky Trinket does this instantly for Great Friends or higher.
  • You get bonus Candy when the two Pokémon were caught far apart — the farther (up to about 100 km), the more Candy.

sections.h: Trade list terms: LF, FT and more
sections.html:
• LF — Looking For: the Pokémon you want (the Looking For side of this list).
  • FT — For Trade: what you can give (the For Trade side).
  • Hundo — a Pokémon with perfect 15/15/15 IVs; shundo is a shiny hundo.
  • Background — a location or special card background shown behind the Pokémon.

sections.h: Share a link and keep several lists
sections.html: Share link creates a URL that opens your list for someone else; they can import it as a new list of their own. With New list you can keep separate lists side by side — for example one for Community Day and one for a regional swap. Lists are saved in your browser, and signing in with Google keeps the same lists on your phone and your computer.

• Special Trades — shiny Pokémon, Legendary Pokémon and Pokémon you have not registered yet — cost more Stardust and are limited to one per day. Higher Friendship levels make them much cheaper.
  • Some Pokémon cannot be traded at all, such as most Mythical Pokémon. The catalogue marks them with 🚫 so you do not advertise something you cannot actually send.
  • Pokémon with a location or special background keep it after the trade, which is why many players put background Pokémon on their lists.
  • Put the trades you care about most in the first rows — most people only glance at the top of an image.

faq.q: Is the trade list generator free?
faq.a: Yes. There is nothing to buy and no sign-up; ads on the page keep the site running.

faq.q: Do I need to log in?
faq.a: No. Your lists are stored in this browser. Logging in with Google is optional and only syncs your lists between devices.

faq.q: Which Pokémon and backgrounds are included?
faq.a: Pokémon released in Pokémon GO with their forms, costumes, shiny and Dynamax/Gigantamax variants, plus the location and special backgrounds that have appeared in events. If a combination is missing, build it yourself with Custom combo.

faq.q: How much Stardust does a Special Trade cost?
faq.a: Between 800 and 1,000,000 Stardust depending on your Friendship level and whether the receiver already has the Pokémon. A Legendary or shiny Pokémon the receiver has not registered costs 1,000,000 at Good Friends and 40,000 at Best Friends.
Shadow Pokémon, most Mythical Pokémon, and any Pokémon you already received in a trade. The catalogue marks untradeable Pokémon with 🚫.

faq.q: Do IVs change after a trade?
faq.a: Yes. IVs are re-rolled when a Pokémon is traded; a higher Friendship level and Lucky Trades raise the minimum.

faq.q: What do LF and FT mean?
faq.a: LF means Looking For (Pokémon you want) and FT means For Trade (Pokémon you can give). This generator puts them in two separate sections of the image.

faq.q: Will my Trainer Code be shown on the image?
faq.a: Only if you type it in. The Trainer Code field is optional and empty by default.
English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German and Spanish. Pokémon names follow the language you choose, and search understands names in all of them.

faq.q: Can I use it on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. On iPhone and Android the finished image can be saved to your photo album or shared directly to another app.
